short_description: Consumer-facing lifestyle trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for sleep-duration tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing sleep trait describing a cautious inherited signal related to longer or shorter habitual sleep duration relative to the current local reference panel.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with habitual sleep-duration tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: This is a cautious panel-relative lifestyle signal, not a direct measurement of how many hours you currently sleep. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a direct readout of how many hours you currently sleep, a sleep-quality score, or medical advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Real-world sleep duration depends strongly on work schedule, stress, caregiving, age, health, medication use, travel, and personal habits.
This trait should not be used as a sleep diagnosis, a sleep-quality assessment, or medical guidance.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
